title.en: Volume 54 Biographies 19: Wang Zhangshu, Li Yan, Yi Louqian, Tian Rengong, Yuan Heng, Du Zheng, Li Che, Cui Peng
title.raw: 卷54 列傳第19 王長述 李衍 伊婁謙 田仁恭 元亨 杜整 李徹 崔彭 Volume 54 Biographies 19: Wang Zhangshu, Li Yan, Yi Louqian, Tian Rengong, Yuan Heng, Du Zheng, Li Che, Cui Peng

sentences.zh: 隋書卷五十四列傳第十九

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 54, Biography 19
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 54, Biography 19

sentences.zh: 王長述

translations.literal: Wang Changshu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changshu

sentences.zh: 王長述，京兆霸城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Changshu was a native of Bacheng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changshu came from Bacheng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖羆，魏太尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pi was Grand Preceptor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pi had been Wei’s grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 父慶遠，周淮州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qingyuan was Governor of Huaizhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingyuan was Zhou’s governor of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 長述幼有儀範，年八歲，周太祖見而異之，曰：「王公有此孫，足為不朽。

translations.literal: From childhood Changshu had dignified bearing. At eight years of age, Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was struck by him, saying: "The Duke Wang has this grandson; that is enough for immortality."
translations.idiomatic: Changshu had dignified bearing even as a child. At eight, Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and marveled, saying, "Duke Wang has this grandson—that alone is enough to make his line immortal."

sentences.zh: 」解褐員外散騎侍郎，封長安縣伯。

translations.literal: He was released from commoner status and made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, enfeoffed as Earl of Chang'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He left commoner status for attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and was enfeoffed as earl of Chang'an county.

sentences.zh: 累遷撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal, and Aide to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to general who pacifies the army, grand master for splendid happiness with the silver seal, and aide to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 長述早孤，少為祖羆所養，及羆薨，居喪過禮，有詔褒異之。

translations.literal: Changshu was orphaned early and was raised by his grandfather Pi. When Pi died, his mourning exceeded the rites, and an edict praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his grandfather Pi; when Pi died his mourning exceeded the rites and an edict singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 免喪，襲封扶風郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the title Duke of Fufeng Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the dukedom of Fufeng with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人，修起居注，改封龍門郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Aide and compiled the Diurnal Records, and his fief was changed to Duke of Longmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed secretariat aide and charged with compiling the diurnal records, he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Longmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 從于謹平江陵有功，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in following Yu Jin in pacifying Jiangling, his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yu Jin in pacifying Jiangling and, for his merit, received an additional five hundred households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，又增邑通前四千七百戶。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication, his fief was again increased, reaching four thousand seven hundred households in all with previous additions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty was founded, his fief grew further to a total of four thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 拜賓部大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of the Guest Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand master of the guest department.

sentences.zh: 出為晉州刺史，轉玉壁總管長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Jizhou and was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Area Commander of Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Jizhou, then became chief clerk under the area commander at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 尋授司憲大夫，出拜廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Grand Master for Law and went out as Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon appointed grand master for law, he went out to serve as governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甚有威惠，吏人懷之，在任數年，蠻夷歸之者三萬餘戶。

translations.literal: He had great authority and grace; officials and people cherished him. In several years in office, more than thirty thousand households of barbarians submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He combined stern authority with kindness, winning the loyalty of officials and commoners alike; within a few years more than thirty thousand barbarian households came over to his rule.

sentences.zh: 朝議嘉之，就拜大將軍。

translations.literal: The court assembly praised this, and he was appointed on the spot as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When the court commended his record, he was promoted on the spot to grand general.

sentences.zh: 後曆襄、仁二州總管，並有能名。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Area Commander of Xiang and Ren prefectures, and in both gained a reputation for capability.
translations.idiomatic: He later held area commands in Xiang and Ren, earning a name for competence in both posts.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，授信州總管，部內夷、獠猶有未賓，長述討平之，進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he was entrusted as Area Commander of Xinzhou. Within his jurisdiction some Yi and Liao tribes had not yet submitted, and Changshu suppressed and pacified them, advancing in rank to Grand General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still chancellor, he was made area commander of Xinzhou; Changshu pacified the unsubmissive Yi and Liao within his district and was promoted to grand general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 王謙作亂益州，遣使致書於長述，因執其使，上其書，又陳取謙之策。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled in Yizhou, he sent a messenger with a letter to Changshu. Changshu thereupon seized the messenger, submitted the letter, and also set forth a plan to capture Qian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rose in rebellion in Yizhou, he sent a messenger with a letter to Changshu; Changshu seized the envoy, forwarded the letter to the throne, and submitted a plan for taking Qian.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，前後賜黃金五百兩，授行軍總管，率眾討謙。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and in succession granted five hundred taels of gold, appointing him Campaign Commander to lead troops to punish Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, rewarded him with five hundred taels of gold in all, and made him campaign commander to lead forces against Qian.

sentences.zh: 以功進位柱國。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was raised to pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，複獻平陳之計，修營戰艦，為上流之師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he again presented a plan to pacify Chen, built and outfitted war-ships, and served as the force of the upper Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he again submitted a plan to conquer Chen, built a fleet of war-ships, and commanded the upstream forces.

sentences.zh: 上善其能，頻加賞勞，下書曰：「每覽高策，深相嘉歎，命將之日，當以公為元帥也。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved of his ability and repeatedly added rewards and commendations, issuing a letter saying: "Whenever I read your lofty plans I deeply admire and praise them. When the day comes to appoint a commander, you shall be made supreme commander."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his talents, showered him with rewards, and wrote: "Your bold plans always win my admiration; when the day comes to appoint a commander-in-chief, it will be you."

sentences.zh: 」後數歲，以行軍總管擊南寧，未至，道病卒。

translations.literal: Several years later, as Campaign Commander he attacked Nanning but died of illness on the road before arriving.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later, while leading a campaign against Nanning as campaign commander, he fell ill on the road and died before reaching his destination.

sentences.zh: 上甚傷惜之，令使者弔祭，贈上柱國、冀州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply grieved and ordered an emissary to offer mourning sacrifices; posthumously he was granted Senior Pillar of the State and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, sent envoys to perform rites of condolence, and posthumously invested him as senior pillar of the state and governor of Jizhou with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子謨嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 謨弟軌，大業末，東郡通守。

translations.literal: Mo's younger brother Gui, at the end of the Daye era, was Prefect of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's younger brother Gui served as prefect of Dong commandery at the end of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 少子文楷，起部郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Wenkai was a Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wenkai was a gentleman in the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: ○李衍

translations.literal: ○ Li Yan
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan

sentences.zh: 李衍，字拔豆，遼東襄平人也。

translations.literal: Li Yan, courtesy name Badou, was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, styled Badou, came from Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父弼，周太師。

translations.literal: His father Bi was Grand Preceptor of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi had been Zhou's grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 衍少專武藝，慷慨有志略。

translations.literal: Yan in youth devoted himself to martial arts, was generous of spirit, and had ambition and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yan devoted himself to martial arts; generous and ambitious, he had both drive and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，釋褐千牛備身，封懷仁縣公。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, he left commoner status as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant and was enfeoffed as Duke of Huairen County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he entered service as a thousand-ox guard attendant and was enfeoffed as duke of Huairen county.

sentences.zh: 加開府，改封普寧縣公，遷義州刺史。

translations.literal: He was granted the Opening of a Government Office, his fief was changed to Duke of Puning County, and he was transferred to Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Granted an opened government office, re-enfeoffed as duke of Puning county, he became governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋從韋孝寬鎮玉壁城，數與賊戰，敵人憚之。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Wei Xiaokuan in garrisoning Yubi fortress, fought the enemy many times, and the enemy feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Wei Xiaokuan in holding Yubi fortress; after many battles with the enemy they came to fear him.

sentences.zh: 及平齊，以軍功進授大將軍，改封真鄉郡公，拜左宮伯，賜雜彩三百匹，奴婢二十口，賜子仲威爵浮陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, for military merit he was promoted and appointed Grand General, his fief changed to Duke of Zhenxiang Commandery; he was appointed Left Palace Guard and granted three hundred lengths of mixed silks, twenty slaves and maidservants, and his son Zhongwei was granted the title Duke of Fuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Qi he was promoted to grand general on account of his military merit, re-enfeoffed as duke of Zhenxiang commandery, and made left palace guard; he received three hundred bolts of colored silk, twenty slaves, and his son Zhongwei was enfeoffed as duke of Fuyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 後曆定、鄜二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Governor of Ding and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Ding and Fu prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 及王謙作亂，高祖以衍為行軍總管，從梁睿擊平之。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, Emperor Wen appointed Yan as Campaign Commander; he followed Liang Rui in attacking and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Emperor Wen made Yan campaign commander and he followed Liang Rui to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，賜縑二千匹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General-in-Chief and granted two thousand bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general-in-chief and given two thousand bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，又以行軍總管討叛蠻，平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, again as Campaign Commander he punished rebellious barbarians and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 1, again as campaign commander, he suppressed rebellious tribes and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國，賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Pillar of the State and granted two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to pillar of the state and given two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校利州總管事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed to inspect and manage the affairs of the Area Commander of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the area command of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥犯塞，以行軍總管率眾討之，不見虜而還。

translations.literal: The next year the Turks raided the frontier; as Campaign Commander he led troops to attack them but returned without encountering the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the Turks raided the border, he led a punitive campaign as campaign commander but found no enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 轉介州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 後數年，朝廷將有事江南，詔衍於襄州道營戰船。

translations.literal: Several years later, when the court planned action against the Jiangnan region, Yan was ordered to build war-ships on the Xiangzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later, as the court prepared for action in the south, Yan was ordered to build warships along the Xiangzhou route.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，授行軍總管，從秦王俊出襄陽道，以功賜帛三千匹，米六百石。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Chen, he was appointed Campaign Commander and followed Prince Qin Jun out by the Xiangyang route; for merit he was granted three thousand bolts of silk and six hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: During the great invasion of Chen he was made campaign commander and marched with Prince Qin Jun via the Xiangyang route; for his achievements he received three thousand bolts of silk and six hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 拜安州總管，頗有惠政，歲餘，以疾還京師，卒于家，時年五十七。

translations.literal: He was appointed Area Commander of Anzhou, had benevolent policies, and after a little more than a year returned to the capital due to illness and died at home, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed area commander of Anzhou, he governed with notable benevolence; a little over a year later illness forced him back to the capital, where he died at home at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子仲威嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhongwei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongwei succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 衍弟子長雅，尚高祖女襄國公主，襲父綸爵，為河陽郡公。

translations.literal: Yan's younger clansman Changya married the Emperor's daughter Princess Xiangguo, inherited his father Lun's title, and was Duke of Heyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger kinsman Changya married Emperor Wen's daughter Princess Xiangguo, inherited his father Lun's title, and held the dukedom of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜將軍、散騎常侍，曆內史侍郎、河州刺史、檢校秦州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed General and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and successively served as Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Governor of Hezhou, and Inspector managing the Area Commander of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he became general and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, later serving as vice minister of the secretariat, governor of Hezhou, and supervisor of the Qinzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 衍從孫密，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yan's grandnephew Mi has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's grandnephew Mi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: ○伊婁謙

translations.literal: ○ Yi Louqian
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian

sentences.zh: 伊婁謙，字彥恭，本鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Yi Louqian, courtesy name Yangong, was originally of Xianbei ethnicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian, styled Yangong, was a Xianbei by origin.

sentences.zh: 其先代為酋長，隨魏南遷。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations were chieftains and migrated south with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had served for generations as tribal chieftains and moved south with the Wei court.

sentences.zh: 祖信，中部太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xin was Administrator of Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xin was administrator of Zhongbu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父靈，相、隆二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ling was Governor of Xiang and Long prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling had been governor of Xiang and Long prefectures.

sentences.zh: 謙性忠直，善辭令。

translations.literal: Qian was by nature loyal and upright and skilled in eloquence and discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was loyal and forthright by nature and gifted with eloquence.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為直閣將軍。

translations.literal: He served Wei as Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wei he served as a direct gate general.

sentences.zh: 周受禪，累遷宣納上士，使持節、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhou received the abdication, he was promoted in succession to Senior Clerk for Proclamations and Reception, Bearing the Staff of Authority as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou dynasty was established he rose through the ranks to senior clerk for proclamations and reception, and held the title general of chariots and cavalry with imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 武帝將伐齊，引入內殿，從容謂曰：「朕將有事戎馬，何者為先？

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to attack Qi, he summoned Qian into the inner hall and said at ease: "I am about to take up arms. Where should I strike first?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu prepared to attack Qi, he summoned Qian to the inner hall and asked casually, "I am about to take the field—where should I strike first?"

sentences.zh: 」謙對曰：「愚臣誠不足以知大事，但偽齊僭擅，跋扈不恭，沈溺倡優，耽昏曲蘖。

translations.literal: Qian replied: "Your foolish subject truly is not enough to know great affairs, but the false Qi usurps and is overbearing and insolent, drowning in actors and singers and sunk in debauchery and wine."
translations.idiomatic: Qian answered, "Your humble servant is hardly fit to counsel on great affairs, but the usurping Qi court is arrogant and insolent, lost in actors and wine and debauchery."

sentences.zh: 其折衝之將斛律明月已斃，讒人之口，上下離心，道路仄目。

translations.literal: Its general who breaks enemy ranks, Hulu Yue, is already dead; slanderers are active and superiors and subordinates are divided in heart; people on the roads narrow their eyes in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Their finest warrior, Hulu Yue, is dead; slander fills the court, rulers and subjects are estranged, and common folk watch the roads in fear.

sentences.zh: 若命六師，臣之願也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty commands the Six Armies, that is this subject's wish.
translations.idiomatic: If you send the six armies, that would be this subject's dearest wish.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，因使謙與小司寇拓拔偉聘齊觀釁。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed heartily and thereupon sent Qian with Junior Minister of Justice Tuoba Wei as envoys to Qi to observe signs of strife.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud and sent Qian with junior minister of justice Tuoba Wei as envoys to Qi to spy out its condition.

sentences.zh: 帝尋發兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon mobilized troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon launched his armies.

sentences.zh: 齊主知之，令其僕射陽休之責謙曰：「貴朝盛夏徵兵，馬首何向？

translations.literal: The Qi ruler learned of this and had his Vice Premier Yang Xiuzhi reproach Qian, saying: "Your noble court is mobilizing troops in midsummer—where are your horses' heads turned?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi ruler learned of this, his vice premier Yang Xiuzhi challenged Qian: "Your court is mobilizing in high summer—where are your armies heading?"

sentences.zh: 」謙答曰：「僕憑式之始，未聞興師。

translations.literal: Qian replied: "From the time I took my post I have not heard of mobilizing armies.
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied, "Since I assumed my post I have heard nothing of any mobilization.

sentences.zh: 設複西增白帝之城，東益巴丘之戍，人情恆理，豈足怪哉！

translations.literal: Even if the west again strengthened the walls of White Emperor City and the east added garrisons at Baqiu, that would be the constant reasoning of human affairs—why should it be surprising!"
translations.idiomatic: If you strengthened White Emperor City in the west and added garrisons at Baqiu in the east, that would be ordinary human prudence—what is strange about that!"

sentences.zh: 」謙參軍高遵以情輸于齊，遂拘留謙不遣。

translations.literal: Qian's staff officer Gao Zun divulged the situation to Qi, whereupon they detained Qian and did not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's aide Gao Zun betrayed their secrets to Qi, and the Qi court detained Qian and refused to release him.

sentences.zh: 帝克并州，召謙勞之曰：「朕之舉兵，本俟卿還；

translations.literal: When the Emperor captured Bingzhou, he summoned Qian to console him, saying: "My mobilizing of armies was originally waiting for your return;
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took Bingzhou he summoned Qian and consoled him: "I had meant to wait until you returned before marching;

sentences.zh: 不圖高遵中為叛逆，乖朕宿心，遵之罪也。

translations.literal: I did not expect that Gao Zun in the middle would prove traitorous, contrary to my long-held intent—the fault is Zun's."
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined Gao Zun would betray us mid-course, thwarting my long-held plan—the fault is Zun's alone."

sentences.zh: 」乃執遵付謙，任令報復。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized Zun and handed him to Qian, leaving revenge entirely to his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zun seized and handed over to Qian, leaving revenge entirely to his discretion.

sentences.zh: 謙頓首請赦之，帝曰：「卿可聚眾唾面，令知愧也。

translations.literal: Qian prostrated himself and begged pardon for him. The Emperor said: "You may gather the crowd to spit in his face and let him know shame."
translations.idiomatic: Qian prostrated himself and begged pardon for Zun. The emperor said, "Gather the men and let them spit in his face—that should teach him shame."

sentences.zh: 」謙跪曰：「以遵之罪，又非唾面之責。

translations.literal: Qian knelt and said: "For Zun's crime, spitting in the face is not the appropriate punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Qian knelt and said, "Zun's crime does not warrant such a punishment as spitting in the face."

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 謙竟待遵如初。

translations.literal: Qian in the end treated Zun as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qian continued to treat Zun exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 其寬厚仁恕，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His magnanimity, kindness, and forbearance were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His magnanimity and kindness were characteristic in just this way.

sentences.zh: 尋賜爵濟陽縣伯，累遷前驅中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the title Earl of Jiyang County and was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon enfeoffed as earl of Jiyang county and rose to grand master of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 大象中，進爵為侯，加位開府。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, he was advanced to Marquis and granted the Opening of a Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang reign he was raised to marquis and granted an opened government office.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，授亳州總管，俄征還京。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he was appointed Area Commander of Bozhou and was soon recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor he was made area commander of Bozhou, then soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既平王謙，謙恥與逆人同名，因爾稱字。

translations.literal: After Wang Qian was pacified, Louqian was ashamed to share a name with the rebel and therefore used his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Qian's rebellion was crushed, Louqian was ashamed to share a name with the traitor and henceforth used his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以彥恭為左武候將軍，俄拜大將軍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he appointed Yangong as Left Commander of the Martial Guard; soon he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne he made Yangong left commander of the martial guard, soon promoted him to grand general and raised him to duke.

sentences.zh: 數年，出為澤州刺史，清約自處，甚得人和。

translations.literal: After several years he went out as Governor of Zezhou, was frugal and restrained in his conduct, and greatly won human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was posted as governor of Zezhou; frugal and self-restrained, he won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，吏人攀戀，行數百里不絕。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of illness; officials and people clung to him in farewell, stretching for several hundred li without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: When illness forced him to retire, officials and townspeople lined the road for hundreds of li to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 數歲，卒于家，時年七十。

translations.literal: After several years he died at home, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he died at home at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: ○田仁恭

translations.literal: ○ Tian Rengong
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rengong

sentences.zh: 田仁恭，字長貴，平涼長城人也。

translations.literal: Tian Rengong, courtesy name Changgui, was a native of Changcheng in Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rengong, styled Changgui, came from Changcheng in Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 父弘，周大司空。

translations.literal: His father Hong was Grand Minister of Works of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong had been Zhou's grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 仁恭性寬仁，有局度。

translations.literal: Rengong was by nature magnanimous and humane and had breadth of vision.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was magnanimous and humane by nature, with breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 在周以明經為掌式中士。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, through mastery of the Classics he became Senior Clerk for Ritual Forms.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he passed the classics examination and became senior clerk for ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 後以父軍功賜爵鶉陰子。

translations.literal: Later for his father's military merit he was granted the title Viscount of Chunyin.
translations.idiomatic: He later received the viscounty of Chunyin in recognition of his father's military achievements.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護引為中外兵曹。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu recruited him as Clerk of Central and External Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand preceptor Yuwen Hu brought him in as clerk of central and external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 後數載，複以父功拜開府儀同三司，遷中外府掾。

translations.literal: Several years later, again for his father's merit he was appointed Grand Master with the Opening of a Government Office with Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies and was transferred to Clerk of the Central and External Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later, again on his father's account, he was made grand master with an opened office of equal honor to the three excellencies and transferred to a clerkship in the central and external offices.

sentences.zh: 從護征伐，數有戰功，改封襄武縣公，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Following Hu on campaigns, he had military merit many times; his fief was changed to Duke of Xiangwu County with a domain of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hu on campaign and won repeated distinction; he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Xiangwu county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，加授上開府，進封淅陽郡公，增邑二千戶，拜幽州總管。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was additionally granted Senior Opening of a Government Office, advanced to Duke of Xiyang Commandery with an increased fief of two thousand households, and appointed Area Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi and was granted senior opened office, raised to duke of Xiyang commandery with an additional two thousand households, and made area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，進爵雁門郡公。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan, he was advanced to Duke of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was raised to duke of Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，征拜小司馬，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he was summoned and appointed Junior Vice Minister of War and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor he was summoned as junior vice minister of war and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 從韋孝寬破尉遲迥于相州，拜柱國。

translations.literal: Following Wei Xiaokuan, he defeated Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou and was appointed Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Jiong at Xiangzhou and was made pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進上柱國，拜太子太師，甚見親重，嘗幸其第，宴飲極歡，禮賜殊厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he was promoted to Senior Pillar of the State and appointed Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince; he was greatly favored and trusted, and the Emperor once visited his residence, feasting with the utmost joy and granting him exceptionally generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was raised to senior pillar of the state and made grand preceptor to the crown prince; greatly favored, he received imperial visits, lavish feasts, and exceptional gifts.

sentences.zh: 奉詔營廟社，進爵觀國公，增邑通前五千戶。

translations.literal: By imperial order he oversaw construction of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, was advanced to Duke of Guan State, and his fief was increased to five thousand households in all with previous additions.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to oversee construction of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, he was raised to duke of Guan state with a total fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made grand general of the right martial guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒官，時年四十七。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died in office, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Minister of Works, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously invested as minister of works with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子世師嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shishi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shishi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 次子德懋，在《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: His second son Demao is treated in the Biography of Filial Devotion and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Demao appears in the Biography of Filial Devotion and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 時有任城郡公王景、鮮虞縣公謝慶恩，並官至上柱國。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Rencheng Wang Jing and Duke of Xianyu Xie Qing'en both held office as Senior Pillars of the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Jing, duke of Rencheng, and Xie Qing'en, duke of Xianyu, both held the rank of senior pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 大義公辛遵及其弟韶，並官至柱國。

translations.literal: Duke of Dayi Xin Zun and his younger brother Shao both reached office as Pillars of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zun, duke of Dayi, and his younger brother Shao both rose to pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其俱佐命功臣，特加崇貴，親禮與仁恭等。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because they were all founding ministers who had aided his rise, specially honored them and treated them with personal courtesy like Rengong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Because they had all aided his rise as founding ministers, Emperor Wen specially honored them and received them with the same personal courtesy as Rengong and the others.

sentences.zh: 事皆亡失雲。

translations.literal: Their affairs have all been lost.
translations.idiomatic: The records of their careers have all been lost.

sentences.zh: ○元亨

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Heng
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Heng

sentences.zh: 元亨，字德良，一名孝才，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Heng, courtesy name Deliang, also named Xiaocai, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Heng, styled Deliang and also known as Xiaocai, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父季海，魏司徒、馮翊王，遇周、齊分隔，季海遂仕長安。

translations.literal: His father Jihai was Minister of Education and King of Fenyang under Wei; when Zhou and Qi were divided, Jihai took office in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jihai had been Wei's minister of education and king of Fenyang; when Zhou and Qi split the realm, Jihai entered service in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 亨時年數歲，與母李氏在洛陽。

translations.literal: Heng was then only a few years old and remained in Luoyang with his mother, Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was then only a few years old and stayed in Luoyang with his mother, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 齊神武帝以亨父在關西，禁錮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenwu of Qi, because Heng's father was in the west, had them placed under confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Because Heng's father was in the west, Emperor Shenwu of Qi had mother and son placed under confinement.

sentences.zh: 其母則魏司空李沖之女也，素有智謀，遂詐稱凍餒，請就食于滎陽。

translations.literal: His mother was the daughter of Wei Minister of Works Li Chong and was by nature resourceful; she therefore feigned hunger and cold and asked to go to Xingyang for food.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a daughter of Wei's minister of works Li Chong, was shrewd by nature; she feigned hunger and cold and asked permission to go to Xingyang for food.

sentences.zh: 齊人以其去關西尚遠，老婦弱子，不以為疑，遂許之。

translations.literal: The Qi people, thinking them still far from the western frontier and only an old woman with a weak child, suspected nothing and granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi authorities, seeing only an old woman and a small boy still far from the western frontier, suspected nothing and granted permission.

sentences.zh: 李氏陰托大豪李長壽，攜亨及孤侄八人，潛行草間，得至長安。

translations.literal: Lady Li secretly entrusted herself to the great magnate Li Changshou, took Heng and eight orphaned nephews, and traveled hidden among the grasslands until they reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li secretly enlisted the great magnate Li Changshou, took Heng and eight orphaned nephews, and traveled by hidden paths until they reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而大悅，以亨功臣子，甚優禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw them and was greatly pleased; because Heng was the son of a founding minister, he treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou was delighted to see them and, because Heng was the son of a founding minister, treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 亨年十二，魏恭帝在儲宮，引為交友。

translations.literal: When Heng was twelve, Emperor Gong of Wei was crown prince and took him as a companion.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, when Emperor Gong of Wei was crown prince, Heng was taken into his circle of companions.

sentences.zh: 釋褐千牛備身。

translations.literal: He left commoner status as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a thousand-ox guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 大統末，襲爵馮翊王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong he inherited the title King of Fenyang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Datong era he inherited the kingship of Fenyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 授拜之日，悲慟不能自勝。

translations.literal: On the day he received the appointment he was overcome with grief and could not contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received the appointment he was overcome with grief and could not contain himself.

sentences.zh: 俄遷通直散騎常侍，曆武衛將軍、勳州刺史，改封平涼王。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with Direct Transmission, and successively served as General of the Martial Guard and Governor of Xunzhou; his title was changed to King of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with direct transmission, later serving as general of the martial guard and governor of Xunzhou before being re-enfeoffed as king of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，例降為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou accepted the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou ascended the throne, by precedent his title was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 明、武時，曆隴州刺史、禦正大夫、小司馬。

translations.literal: Under Emperors Ming and Wu he successively served as Governor of Longzhou, Grand Master for Rectification, and Junior Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Ming and Wu he served in succession as governor of Longzhou, grand master for rectification, and junior vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，遇尉遲迥作亂，洛陽人梁康、邢流水等舉兵應迥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong rebelled; the men of Luoyang Liang Kang, Xing Liushui, and others raised troops in response to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor, Yuwen Jiong rebelled; Liang Kang, Xing Liushui, and other men of Luoyang raised troops in support of him.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，眾至萬餘。

translations.literal: Within ten days their force reached more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days their force swelled to more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 州治中王文舒潛與梁康相結，將圖亨。

translations.literal: The prefectural aide Wang Wenshu secretly joined with Liang Kang and planned to seize Heng.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural aide Wang Wenshu secretly colluded with Liang Kang and plotted against Heng.

sentences.zh: 亨陰知其謀，乃選關中兵，得二千人為左右，執文舒斬之，以兵襲擊梁康、邢流水，皆破之。

translations.literal: Heng secretly learned of the plot, selected two thousand troops from Guanzhong as his personal guard, seized Wenshu and executed him, then attacked Liang Kang and Xing Liushui and defeated them both.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the plot in secret, Heng selected two thousand Guanzhong troops as his guard, seized Wenshu and executed him, then attacked Liang Kang and Xing Liushui and routed them both.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，征拜太常卿，增邑七百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, Heng was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and his fief was increased by seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Heng was summoned as minister of ceremonies and his fief was increased by seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋出為衛州刺史，加大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Weizhou and was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as governor of Weizhou and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 衛土俗薄，亨以威嚴鎮之，在職八年，風化大洽。

translations.literal: The people of Wei were shallow in custom; Heng governed them with stern authority, and in eight years in office local customs were greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei were morally lax; Heng governed with stern authority, and in eight years local customs were thoroughly reformed.

sentences.zh: 後以老病，表乞骸骨，吏人詣闕上表，請留臥治，上嗟歎者久之。

translations.literal: Later, due to age and illness, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; officials and people went to the palace to submit memorials asking that he remain and govern from his bed, and the Emperor sighed over this for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted by age and illness, he requested retirement; officials and townspeople petitioned the throne to let him remain and govern from his bed, and the emperor sighed over this at length.

sentences.zh: 其年，亨以篤疾，重請還京，上令使者致醫藥，問動靜，相望於道。

translations.literal: That year, as Heng's illness grew grave, he again asked to return to the capital; the Emperor sent envoys with medicine and inquiries, one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as his illness grew grave, he again asked to return to the capital; the emperor sent envoys with medicine and inquiries in an unbroken stream along the road.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒于家，時年六十九。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died at home, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at home at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: ○杜整

translations.literal: ○ Du Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng

sentences.zh: 杜整，字皇育，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Zheng, courtesy name Huangyu, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng, styled Huangyu, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖盛，魏直閣將軍、潁川太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng was Direct Gate General and Administrator of Yingchuan under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng had been a direct gate general and administrator of Yingchuan under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父辟，渭州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Pi was Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi had been governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 整少有風概，九歲丁父憂，哀毀骨立，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Zheng from youth had force of character; at nine he entered mourning for his father, grieving until his bones showed, and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zheng had force of character; at nine he mourned his father until his frame was wasted away, and he was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 及長，驍勇有膂力，好讀孫、吳《兵法》。

translations.literal: When grown he was bold and brave with great physical strength and loved to read the military treatises of Sunzi and Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was bold and physically powerful and loved to read the military treatises of Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，襲爵武鄉侯。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong under Wei he inherited the title Marquis of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wei Datong era he inherited the marquisate of Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 周太祖引為親信。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou recruited him as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou brought him in as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 後事宇文護子中山公訓，甚被親遇。

translations.literal: Later he served Yuwen Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Yuwen Hu's son, Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 俄授都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed colonel.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，為內侍上士，累遷儀同三司，拜武州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Senior Attendant of the Inner Service and was promoted in succession to Grand Master with Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies, then appointed Governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was senior attendant of the inner service, rose to grand master with equal honor to the three excellencies, and was made governor of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，加上儀同，進爵平原縣公，邑千戶，入為勳曹中大夫。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was granted Senior Equal Honor, advanced to Duke of Pingyuan County with a fief of one thousand households, and entered service as Grand Master of the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, was granted senior equal honor, raised to duke of Pingyuan county with a fief of one thousand households, and entered the capital as grand master of the bureau of merits.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，進位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, he was promoted to the Opening of a Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor he was granted an opened government office.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，加上開府，進封長廣郡公，俄拜左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the abdication was accepted he was granted Senior Opening, advanced to Duke of Changguang Commandery, and soon appointed General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne changed hands he was granted senior opened office, raised to duke of Changguang commandery, and soon made general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，以母憂去職，起令視事。

translations.literal: After several years in office he resigned on account of mourning for his mother but was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he resigned to mourn his mother but was recalled and ordered to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年，突厥犯塞，詔遣衛王爽總戎北伐，以整為行軍總管兼元帥長史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; an edict dispatched Prince Wei Shuang to command the northern campaign, with Zheng as Campaign Commander and chief of staff to the supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 6, when the Turks raided the frontier, Prince Wei Shuang was ordered to command the northern campaign and Zheng was made campaign commander and chief of staff to the supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 至合川，無虜而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Hechuan, they found no enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Hechuan, found no enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 整密進取陳之策，上善之，於是以行軍總管鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Zheng secretly submitted a plan to capture Chen; the Emperor approved it and thereupon appointed him Campaign Commander to garrison Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng secretly submitted a plan to conquer Chen; the emperor approved it and made him campaign commander at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而傷之，贈帛四百匹，米四百石，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it he was grieved and granted four hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was grieved at the news, granted four hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子楷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 官至開府。

translations.literal: He reached office as Grand Master with the Opening of a Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master with an opened government office.

sentences.zh: 整弟肅，亦少有志行。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Su also from youth had ambition and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother Su also showed ambition and integrity from youth.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，為通直散騎常侍、北地太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with Direct Transmission and Prefect of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with direct transmission and prefect of Beidi.

sentences.zh: ○李徹

translations.literal: ○ Li Che
translations.idiomatic: Li Che

sentences.zh: 李徹，字廣達，朔方岩綠人也。

translations.literal: Li Che, courtesy name Guangda, was a native of Yanlü in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Che, styled Guangda, came from Yanlü in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 父和，開皇初為柱國。

translations.literal: His father He became Pillar of the State at the beginning of Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: His father He became pillar of the state at the beginning of Kaihuang.

sentences.zh: 徹性剛毅，有器幹，偉容儀，多武藝。

translations.literal: Che was by nature resolute and firm, had capacity and ability, possessed a imposing appearance, and was skilled in many martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Che was resolute and firm by nature, capable and imposing in bearing, and skilled in many martial arts.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護引為親信，尋拜殿中司馬，累遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu recruited him as a trusted intimate; soon he was appointed Palace Attendant Major and was promoted in succession to Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Grand preceptor Yuwen Hu brought him in as a trusted intimate; he was soon made palace attendant major and rose to commandant of the imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 護以徹謹厚有才具，甚禮之。

translations.literal: Hu, because Che was careful, honest, and talented, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Che was careful, honest, and talented, Hu treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 護子中山公訓為蒲州刺史，護令徹以本官從焉。

translations.literal: Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun was Governor of Puzhou, and Hu ordered Che to accompany him in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's son, Duke of Zhongshan Xun, was governor of Puzhou, and Hu ordered Che to accompany him in his existing office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Master with Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made general of chariots and cavalry with equal honor to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，從皇太子西征吐谷渾，以功賜爵同昌縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he followed the Crown Prince on the western campaign against Tuyuhun and for merit was granted the title Viscount of Tongchang County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he followed the crown prince on the western campaign against Tuyuhun and for his merit was enfeoffed as viscount of Tongchang county with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後從帝拔晉州。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in capturing Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the emperor in capturing Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 及帝班師，徹與齊王憲屯雞棲原。

translations.literal: When the Emperor withdrew the army, Che and Prince of Qi Xian encamped at Jiqiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew, Che and Prince of Qi Xian encamped at Jiqiyuan.

sentences.zh: 齊主高緯以大軍至，憲引兵西上，以避其鋒。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler Gao Wei arrived with a great army; Xian led his troops westward to avoid their spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler Gao Wei arrived with a great army; Xian led his troops westward to avoid their spearhead.

sentences.zh: 緯遣其驍將賀蘭豹子率勁騎躡憲，戰于晉州城北。

translations.literal: Wei sent his fierce general Helan Baozi with crack cavalry to pursue Xian; they fought north of Jizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent his fierce general Helan Baozi with crack cavalry to pursue Xian, and they fought north of Jizhou city.

sentences.zh: 憲師敗，徹與楊素、宇文慶等力戰，憲軍賴以獲全。

translations.literal: Xian's army was defeated; Che, Yang Su, Yuwen Qing, and others fought fiercely, and Xian's army was preserved intact thanks to them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's army was defeated; Che, Yang Su, Yuwen Qing, and others fought fiercely and preserved Xian's army intact.

sentences.zh: 複從帝破齊師於汾北，乘勝下高壁，拔晉陽，擒高湝于冀州，俱有力焉。

translations.literal: Again he followed the Emperor in defeating Qi forces north of the Fen River, pressed the victory to take Gaobi, captured Jinyang, and at Jizhou seized Gao Huan—all with notable contribution.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor in defeating Qi forces north of the Fen River, pressed the victory to take Gaobi and Jinyang, and helped capture Gao Huan at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，加開府，別封蔡陽縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Recording his earlier and later merit, he was granted the Opening of a Government Office and separately enfeoffed as Duke of Caiyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative achievements he was granted an opened government office and separately enfeoffed as duke of Caiyang county with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，從韋孝寬略定淮南，每為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and each time served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and always served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 及淮南平，即授淮州刺史，安集初附，甚得其歡心。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified he was immediately appointed Governor of Huaizhou and settled the newly submitted population, greatly winning their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified he was immediately made governor of Huaizhou; he settled the newly submitted population and greatly won their hearts.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加上開府，轉雲州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, he was granted Senior Opening and transferred to Governor of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was granted senior opened office and transferred to governor of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，征為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he was summoned as General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was summoned as general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣之鎮并州也，朝廷妙選正人有文武才幹者，為之僚佐。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Bingzhou, the court carefully selected upright men with both civil and military talent to serve as his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Bingzhou, the court carefully selected upright men of civil and military talent for his staff.

sentences.zh: 上以徹前代舊臣，數持軍旅，詔徹總晉王府軍事，進爵齊安郡公。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Che was an old minister of the previous dynasty who had often held military command, ordered him to oversee all military affairs of the Prince of Jin's household and advanced him to Duke of Qi'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Che was an old minister who had often held military command, the emperor ordered him to oversee all military affairs of Prince Jin's household and raised him to duke of Qi'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀亦鎮益州，上謂侍臣曰：「安得文同王子相，武如李廣達者乎？

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu was also stationed at Yizhou; the Emperor said to his attendants: "Where can I find a civil adviser like Wang Zixiang and a military one like Li Guangda?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu was also stationed at Yizhou; the emperor said to his attendants, "Where can I find a civil adviser like Wang Zixiang and a military one like Li Guangda?"

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥沙缽略可汗犯塞，上令衛王爽為元帥，率眾擊之，以徹為長史。

translations.literal: The next year the Turkic qaghan Shaboluoe raided the frontier; the Emperor appointed Prince Wei Shuang supreme commander to lead troops against him, with Che as chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Turkic qaghan Shaboluoe raided the frontier; the emperor made Prince Wei Shuang supreme commander and Che his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 遇虜于白道，行軍總管李充言於爽曰：「周、齊之世，有同戰國，中夏力分，其來久矣。

translations.literal: They encountered the enemy at Baidao; Campaign Commander Li Chong said to Shuang: "In the eras of Zhou and Qi it was like the Warring States period—the Central Lands were divided in strength, and this has long been so.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered the enemy at Baidao; campaign commander Li Chong said to Shuang, "In the Zhou and Qi eras the realm was divided like the Warring States period, and this has long been so.

sentences.zh: 突厥每侵邊，諸將輒以全軍為計，莫能死戰。

translations.literal: Whenever the Turks raided the frontier, generals always made preserving the whole army their plan and none would fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Turks raided the frontier, generals always made preserving the whole army their plan and none would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 由是突厥勝多敗少，所以每輕中國之師。

translations.literal: Hence the Turks won more often than they lost, and so they always looked down on the armies of the Central Lands.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Turks won more often than they lost and always looked down on Chinese armies.

sentences.zh: 今者沙缽略悉國內之眾，屯據要險，必輕我而無備，精兵襲之，可破也。

translations.literal: Now Shaboluoe has mobilized all the forces within his realm and holds strategic passes; he is sure to underestimate us and be unprepared—a strike with elite troops can break him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shaboluoe has mobilized all his forces and holds the strategic passes; he is sure to underestimate us and be unprepared—a strike with elite troops can break him.

sentences.zh: 」爽從之。

translations.literal: Shuang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 諸將多以為疑，唯徹獎成其計，請與同行。

translations.literal: Most of the generals were doubtful, but only Che encouraged the plan and asked to go with them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the generals were doubtful, but Che alone encouraged the plan and asked to go with them.

sentences.zh: 遂與充率精騎五千，出其不意，掩擊大破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Chong led five thousand elite cavalry, caught the enemy unawares, and struck them in a surprise attack, routing them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Che and Chong then led five thousand elite cavalry, caught the enemy unawares, and routed them completely in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略棄所服金甲，潛草中而遁。

translations.literal: Shaboluoe abandoned the golden armor he was wearing and fled hidden in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Shaboluoe abandoned the golden armor he was wearing and fled hidden in the grass.

sentences.zh: 以功加上大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to grand general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 沙缽略因此屈膝稱籓。

translations.literal: Because of this Shaboluoe bowed in submission and declared himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Shaboluoe bowed in submission and declared himself a vassal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，沙缽略為阿拔所侵，上疏請援。

translations.literal: Before long Shaboluoe was invaded by Aba and submitted a memorial requesting aid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shaboluoe was invaded by Aba and submitted a memorial requesting aid.

sentences.zh: 以徹為行軍總管，率精騎一萬赴之。

translations.literal: Che was appointed Campaign Commander and led ten thousand elite cavalry to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Che was made campaign commander and led ten thousand elite cavalry to his relief.

sentences.zh: 阿拔聞而遁去。

translations.literal: When Aba heard of it he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Che's approach, Aba fled.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，複領行軍總管，屯平涼以備胡寇，封安道郡公。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Che again held the post of Campaign Commander, encamped at Pingliang to guard against barbarian raiders, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Andao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Che again served as campaign commander, encamped at Pingliang against barbarian raids, and was enfeoffed as duke of Andao commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he was promoted to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 10 he was raised to pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣轉牧淮海，以徹為揚州總管司馬，改封德廣郡公。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang was transferred to govern the Huaihai region, Che was appointed Chief Administrator to the Area Commander of Yangzhou and his title was changed to Duke of Deguang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin Guang was transferred to govern the Huaihai region, Che was made chief administrator to the Yangzhou area command and re-enfeoffed as duke of Deguang commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋徙封城陽郡公。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was moved to Duke of Chengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon re-enfeoffed as duke of Chengyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥犯塞，徹複領行軍總管擊破之。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Turks raided the frontier, Che again served as Campaign Commander and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks raided the frontier, Che again served as campaign commander and routed them.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲之得罪也，以徹素與熲相善，因被疏忌，不復任使。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Premier Gao Jiong fell from grace, because Che had long been on good terms with Jiong he was distanced and distrusted and was no longer given assignments.
translations.idiomatic: When left vice premier Gao Jiong fell from grace, Che was distanced and distrusted because of his long friendship with Jiong and received no further assignments.

sentences.zh: 後出怨言，上聞而召之，入臥內賜宴，言及平生，因遇鴆而卒。

translations.literal: Later he uttered resentful words; when the Emperor heard of it he summoned him, entertained him in the inner chamber, spoke of their lives together, and thereupon had him meet poisoned wine and die.
translations.idiomatic: Later he uttered resentful words; when the emperor heard of it he summoned him, entertained him in the inner chamber, spoke of their lives together, and had him drink poisoned wine and die.

sentences.zh: 大業中，其妻宇文氏為孽子安遠誣以咒詛，伏誅。

translations.literal: During the Daye era his wife, of the Yuwen clan, was falsely accused of sorcery and curses by the illegitimate son Anyuan and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era his wife of the Yuwen clan was falsely accused of sorcery by the illegitimate son Anyuan and was executed.

sentences.zh: ○崔彭

translations.literal: ○ Cui Peng
translations.idiomatic: Cui Peng

sentences.zh: 崔彭，字子彭，博陵安平人也。

translations.literal: Cui Peng, courtesy name Zipeng, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Peng, styled Zipeng, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，魏殷州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Governor of Yinzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai had been governor of Yinzhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父謙，周荊州總管。

translations.literal: His father Qian was Area Commander of Jingzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian had been area commander of Jingzhou under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 彭少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Peng was orphaned young and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Peng was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 性剛毅，有武略，工騎射。

translations.literal: He was resolute and firm by nature, had military stratagem, and was skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Resolute and firm by nature, he had military stratagem and was skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 善《周官》、《尚書》，略通大義。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Documents and had a general grasp of their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou and the Book of Documents and had a general grasp of their meaning.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為侍伯上士，累轉門正上士。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Senior Attendant of the Palace Guard and was transferred in succession to Senior Attendant of the Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was senior attendant of the palace guard and rose to senior attendant of the gate guard.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，周陳王純鎮齊州，高祖恐純為變，遣彭以兩騎征純入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Chancellor, Prince Chen Chun of Zhou was stationed at Qizhou; the Emperor feared Chun might rebel and dispatched Peng with two mounted escorts to summon Chun to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was chancellor, Prince Chen Chun of Zhou was stationed at Qizhou; fearing rebellion, the emperor sent Peng with two mounted escorts to summon Chun to court.

sentences.zh: 彭未至齊州三十裡，因詐病，止傳舍，遣人謂純曰：「天子有詔書至王所，彭苦疾，不能強步，願王降臨之。

translations.literal: When Peng was still thirty li from Qizhou he feigned illness, stopped at a relay station, and sent a man to tell Chun: "The Son of Heaven has an edict arriving at Your Highness's place; Peng suffers severe illness and cannot force himself to walk—Your Highness, please come down to me."
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Qizhou Peng feigned illness, stopped at a relay station, and sent word to Chun: "The Son of Heaven has an edict for Your Highness; Peng is too ill to walk—please come to me."

sentences.zh: 」純疑有變，多將從騎至彭所。

translations.literal: Chun suspected something amiss and brought many mounted followers to Peng's place.
translations.idiomatic: Chun suspected trouble and came with many mounted followers.

sentences.zh: 彭出傳舍迎之，察純有疑色，恐不就征，因詐純曰：「王可避人，將密有所道。

translations.literal: Peng came out of the relay station to meet him, saw suspicion on Chun's face, and fearing he would not obey the summons, therefore deceived Chun, saying: "Your Highness may dismiss your attendants; I have something confidential to convey."
translations.idiomatic: Peng came out to meet him, saw suspicion on Chun's face, and fearing refusal, deceived him: "Your Highness may dismiss your attendants—I have something confidential to say."

sentences.zh: 」純麾從騎，彭又曰：「將宣詔，王可下馬。

translations.literal: Chun waved his followers away; Peng again said: "I am about to proclaim the edict—Your Highness may dismount."
translations.idiomatic: Chun dismissed his followers; Peng said again, "I am about to proclaim the edict—Your Highness should dismount."

sentences.zh: 」純遽下，彭顧其騎士曰：「陳王不從詔征，可執也。

translations.literal: Chun hurriedly dismounted; Peng turned to his horsemen and said: "Prince Chen refuses the edict summoning him to court—seize him."
translations.idiomatic: Chun hurriedly dismounted; Peng turned to his horsemen and said, "Prince Chen refuses the summons—seize him."

sentences.zh: 」騎士因執而鎖之。

translations.literal: The horsemen thereupon seized and shackled him.
translations.idiomatic: The horsemen seized and shackled him.

sentences.zh: 彭乃大言曰：「陳王有罪，詔征入朝，左右不得輒動。

translations.literal: Peng then declared loudly: "Prince Chen is guilty; by edict he is summoned to court—attendants may not move rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Peng then declared loudly, "Prince Chen is guilty; by edict he is summoned to court—attendants must not move."

sentences.zh: 」其從者愕然而去。

translations.literal: His followers stood stunned and departed.
translations.idiomatic: His followers stood stunned and departed.

sentences.zh: 高祖見而大悅，拜上儀同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen saw this he was greatly pleased and appointed Peng Senior Equal Honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and made Peng senior equal honor.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷監門郎將，兼領右衛長史，賜爵安陽縣男。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to Commandant of the Gate Guard and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Right Guard, and was granted the title Viscount of Anyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, Peng became commandant of the gate guard and chief administrator of the right guard, and was enfeoffed as viscount of Anyang county.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉車騎將軍，俄轉驃騎，恆典宿衛。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, soon to General of Fast Cavalry, and constantly held charge of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he became general of chariots and cavalry, then general of fast cavalry, and constantly held charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 性謹密，在省闥二十餘年，每當上在仗，危坐終日，未嘗有怠惰之容，上甚嘉之。

translations.literal: He was careful and discreet by nature; for more than twenty years in the inner precincts, whenever the Emperor was on duty with arms he sat upright all day and never showed a negligent bearing, and the Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and discreet by nature, for more than twenty years in the inner precincts he sat upright all day whenever the emperor was on armed duty and never showed negligence; the emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 上每謂彭曰：「卿當上日，我寢處自安。

translations.literal: The Emperor often said to Peng: "On the days you are on duty I sleep at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often told Peng, "On the days you are on duty I sleep at ease."

sentences.zh: 」又嘗曰：「卿弓馬固以絕人，頗知學不？

translations.literal: He also once said: "Your bow and horse skills are truly unmatched—do you know anything of learning?"
translations.idiomatic: He also once asked, "Your bow and horse skills are truly unmatched—do you know anything of learning?"

sentences.zh: 」彭曰：「臣少愛《周禮》、《尚書》，每於休沐之暇，不敢廢也。

translations.literal: Peng replied: "Your subject from youth has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Documents, and in the leisure of rest days I have never neglected them."
translations.idiomatic: Peng replied, "Your subject has loved the Rites of Zhou and the Book of Documents from youth, and never neglects them even on rest days."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「試為我言之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Try telling me something of them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then tell me something of them."

sentences.zh: 」彭因說君臣戒慎之義，上稱善。

translations.literal: Peng thereupon expounded the doctrine of vigilance between ruler and minister, and the Emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Peng expounded the doctrine of vigilance between ruler and minister, and the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 觀者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those who witnessed it considered his words well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who witnessed it considered his words well chosen.

sentences.zh: 後加上開府，遷備身將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was granted Senior Opening and transferred to General of the Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later granted senior opened office and made general of the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宴達頭可汗使者于武德殿，有鴿鳴于梁上。

translations.literal: The Emperor once entertained the envoy of Qaghan Datou at Wude Hall; a pigeon cried on a beam above.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once entertained the envoy of Qaghan Datou at Wude Hall when a pigeon cried on a beam above.

sentences.zh: 上命彭射之，既發而中。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Peng to shoot it; as soon as he released the arrow he hit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Peng to shoot it; his arrow struck true on release.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賜錢一萬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and granted ten thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted ten thousand coins.

sentences.zh: 及使者反，可汗複遣使於上曰：「請得崔將軍一與相見。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the qaghan again sent an envoy to the Emperor saying: "I request to meet General Cui once."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the qaghan sent another envoy saying, "I request to meet General Cui once."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此必善射聞於虜庭，所以來請耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This must be because his skill in archery is known in the barbarian court—that is why they come to request him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "His skill in archery must be known in the barbarian court—that is why they ask for him."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Peng at once.

sentences.zh: 及至匈奴中，可汗召善射者數十人，因擲肉於野，以集飛鳶，遣其善射者射之，多不中。

translations.literal: When he reached the Xiongnu lands, the qaghan summoned several dozen skilled archers, threw meat into the wild to gather flying kites, and had his skilled archers shoot at them—most missed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Xiongnu lands, the qaghan summoned several dozen skilled archers, threw meat into the wild to gather flying kites, and had them shoot—most missed.

sentences.zh: 複請彭射之，彭連發數矢，皆應弦而落，突厥相顧，莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: He again asked Peng to shoot; Peng released several arrows in succession and each fell at the twang of the string; the Turks looked at one another and all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Peng was asked to shoot again; he released several arrows in succession and each kite fell at the twang of the string; the Turks looked at one another in admiration.

sentences.zh: 可汗留彭不遣百餘日，上賂以繒彩，然後得歸。

translations.literal: The qaghan detained Peng for more than a hundred days; the Emperor bribed them with silks and only then was he allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan detained Peng for more than a hundred days; the emperor sent silks as ransom before he was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，進爵安陽縣公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou he was advanced to Duke of Anyang County with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era he was raised to duke of Anyang county with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Peng was transferred to Grand General of the Left Forward Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Peng was made grand general of the left forward command.

sentences.zh: 從幸洛陽，彭督後軍。

translations.literal: Accompanying the Emperor on a visit to Luoyang, Peng commanded the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Luoyang, Peng commanded the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 時漢王諒初平，餘黨往往屯聚，令彭率眾數萬鎮遏山東，複領慈州事。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Han Liang had just been pacified and remnant factions were often gathering; the Emperor ordered Peng to lead several tens of thousands of men to suppress the east of the mountains and again to hold charge of Cizhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Han Liang just pacified and remnant factions gathering, the emperor ordered Peng to lead tens of thousands of men to suppress the east of the mountains and again to hold charge of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以其清，賜絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his integrity, granted five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him five hundred bolts of silk for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使弔祭，贈大將軍，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched an envoy to offer mourning sacrifices and posthumously granted him Grand General with the posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to mourn him and posthumously invested him as grand general with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 子寶德嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baode succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baode succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王長述等，或出總方嶽，或入司禁旅，鹹著聲績，以功名終，有以取之也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wang Changshu and the others, whether governing the provinces or serving in the palace guard, all achieved renown and ended their careers in merit and fame—they had what it took to win such outcomes.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Wang Changshu and the others, whether governing provinces or serving in the palace guard, all won renown and ended in merit and fame—they had what it took.

sentences.zh: 伊婁謙志量弘遠，不念舊惡，請赦高遵之罪，有國士之風焉。

translations.literal: Yi Louqian had far-reaching ambition and breadth of mind; he did not bear old grudges and begged pardon for Gao Zun's crime—he had the bearing of a true gentleman of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Louqian had far-reaching ambition and breadth of mind; he did not bear old grudges and begged pardon for Gao Zun—he had the bearing of a true gentleman of the realm.

sentences.zh: 崔彭巡警岩廊，毅然難犯，禦侮之寄，有足稱乎！

translations.literal: Cui Peng patrolled the imperial halls, stern and unassailable; in the charge of warding off insult, he is well worth praising!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Peng patrolled the imperial halls, stern and unassailable; as a guardian against insult, he is well worth praising!
